attributes.context: The clause appears in Section 15.7 - Training, and the same section limits this language to employees in the Systems Operation Work Group within the Transmission and Distribution Section of Tacoma Power and adds a one-hour minimum plus exclusions for meals, travel time, premium pay, fatigue time, or other associated compensation.

extraction_text: When management has identified a need to provide specific training or schedule a meeting (e.g. safety meetings, staff meetings, new equipment briefings, etc.) that is outside the employee's normal work hours and participation is voluntary, the employer will compensate the employee at the applicable overtime rate for all time that the employee is in attendance.

attributes.context: This appears in a Letter of Understanding on Work Assignment Flexibility between the City of Tacoma Department of Public Utilities, Tacoma Power, and IBEW Local 483. The surrounding item addresses meter and relays with integrated internal communication functions and seeks to reduce redundancy and assign tasks efficiently by qualified, journey-level, trained employees.

extraction_text: It is expected that the Communication, and Meter Relay work groups will work cooperatively to determine suitability, communications exchange criteria and compatibility of a new piece of equipment before it's introduced into the system. When a new piece of equipment is introduced into the system, Union and Management will form a group to review areas of overlap.

attributes.context: The surrounding Letter of Understanding between Tacoma Power and IBEW Local 483 addresses work assignment flexibility for the Wynoochee River Project, where specialized powerhouse and switchyard equipment includes plant control systems and work may be performed by specified employees or contractors.

extraction_text: New installations of electrical and mechanical equipment will be the responsibility of Hydro Project Electricians, Hydro Project Mechanics or a contractor.
